answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
